transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what finally made me call the employee assistance program at work is that I’m just barely sleeping right. I'll lie there at night replaying things from work, or arguments I've had at home... and then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. By the time I actually have to start my day, I feel like I never really rested at all.
Do you feel anxious or on edge during the day?

Not really, no. I mean, work is always a little stressful, but I wouldn't say I feel anxious or on edge. Mostly, I just feel... drained. Because of the sleep thing, I just kind of drag myself through the day. But I don't get that nervous or keyed-up feeling, if that's what you mean.
Has something particularly stressful or traumatic happened to you recently?

No, not really. I mean, nothing out of the ordinary. Work is... well, I'm a sales manager, so there are always quotas and deadlines to hit, but it's nothing I haven't been dealing with for years. There hasn't been any big trauma or major life changes recently, if that's what you mean. Just the usual day-to-day stuff.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's like this heavy, gray mood just kind of follows me around. Most days, it's there when I'm at the office, it's there in the car on the way back, and it's there when I get home. Even when nothing in particular is going wrong, I just feel... I don't know, kind of hollow inside. It's just this constant, low-level sadness that I can't seem to shake.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family?

Not really, no. I used to really look forward to things, you know? Like, I'd play pickup basketball, go to bowling nights, hit up music festivals... I even used to love firing up the smoker and having friends over. But lately... I just don't care. I end up canceling a lot of the time. And even when I do go, it just feels like I'm going through the motions. I'm there, but I'm not really getting anything out of it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I'd say it's been... probably about a year and two months now. Yeah, right around then. That's kind of when the arguments at home started getting a lot worse, and... well, it's just been going on since then.
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure from activities that normally bring you joy?

Yeah, I think that's what I was getting at a minute ago. Like with the basketball and the bowling... I just don't get any joy out of them anymore. Even when I force myself to do those things, the pleasure just isn't there.
Has this feeling of sadness and loss of interest in activities been constant over the past year and two months, or have you had periods where you felt better?

It's been pretty constant, honestly. Most days I just feel like this heavy, gray mood follows me around. It's with me at the office, in the car, back at the house... and even when nothing specific is happening or going wrong, I just feel kind of hollow. So, yeah, I haven't really had any periods where it lifts or I feel back to normal.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you felt significantly better over the past year and two months?

No, definitely not. Like I was just saying, it's been pretty much non-stop. I haven't had any stretch like that... definitely not two whole months where I felt back to normal or significantly better. It's just been this same low feeling the entire time.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Not really, no. Like I mentioned with the basketball and bowling... the enjoyment is just gone. And it's the same for other things I used to really look forward to. I used to love going to music festivals, or just firing up the smoker to cook for friends on the weekends. But lately, I either just cancel my plans, or if I do show up, I feel like I'm just going through the motions. So, no, I can't really think of anything I actually find pleasure in right now.
Has your low mood or loss of interest in activities lasted for two years or more?

No, not two years. Like I was saying, it's been about a year and two months. That's when things really started going downhill... the arguments at home started getting a lot worse around then, and this feeling has just stuck with me since.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms seemed to improve for at least a couple of weeks at any point over the past year and two months?

No, I haven't. Even for just a couple of weeks, it's... it's just been pretty constant. I can't think of any time where things felt like they were lifting or getting any better since this all started.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

I think we just talked about that, actually. But, uh, no. Like I said a minute ago, there's really nothing. Not the basketball, not the cooking... I just don't have anything I look forward to or get any enjoyment out of right now.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms seemed to improve for at least two months at any point over the past year and two months?

No, not at all. Like I mentioned a second ago, it's been pretty constant this whole time. Ever since this started about a year and two months ago, right when all those arguments at home got worse... it's just been steady. No breaks, definitely not for two months.
Have you had any periods where you felt completely back to your normal self for at least two months since your symptoms started?

I feel like we're kind of repeating the same question, but... no. No, I haven't felt completely back to normal, either. There hasn't been any two-month stretch—or any stretch, really—where I felt like myself again since this all started. It's just been the same the whole time.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms seemed to improve for at least a few months at any point since they started?
I... yeah, I'm pretty sure that's the exact same question again. But, no. Like I just said, there haven't been any months where things improved. It's just been constant this whole time.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms seemed to improve for at least 2 months, but then returned?

Look, I really don't mean to be difficult, but... it's still no. I know you probably have a list of questions you have to get through, but my answer hasn't changed. I haven't had any two-month period where things got better and then came back. It's just been a straight line of feeling this way the entire time.
